extracted.intended_audience: corporate clients, in-house and outside counsel, compliance officers, and practitioners tracking False Claims Act enforcement
extracted.subtask_description: A short client-alert style summary of Department of Justice False Claims Act statistics and enforcement trends for Fiscal Year 2024, highlighting total recoveries, industry breakdowns, notable enforcement initiatives, and exemplar settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCA settlements and judgments total
rubrics_metrics.description: FCA settlements and judgments exceeded $2.9 billion in FY 2024, an increase from the $2.68 billion recovered in FY 2023; more than $2.4 billion of all recoveries resulted from settlements and judgments in qui tam lawsuits, and whistleblowers received over $400 million in FY 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use total dollar recoveries as a headline metric; when reporting, note year-over-year comparisons. Be explicit whether figures include or exclude state program recoveries (the headline $2.9B here does not include recoveries for state Medicaid programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry concentration — healthcare
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlements in the healthcare industry accounted for over $1.67 billion or roughly 58% of FY 2024 settlements and judgments, involving managed care providers, hospitals and other medical facilities, pharmacies, pharmaceutical companies, laboratories, and physicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing FCA activity, break out industry-specific recoveries (healthcare is frequently dominant). Note related actions (e.g., anti‑kickback and opioid-related claims) and any additional recoveries for state Medicaid programs that may not be included in DOJ's headline figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whistleblower (qui tam) filings and recoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: More whistleblower qui tam lawsuits were filed in FY 2024 than in any prior year, representing a 38% increase over the prior year’s total; FY 2024 averaged 18 new qui tam cases filed each week. Of the $2.9 billion recovered, $2.4 billion arose from whistleblower qui tam suits, and whistleblowers received over $400 million in relator shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track both filing volume (new qui tam suits) and dollar recoveries attributable to qui tam actions; emphasize relator shares as a separate sub-metric. Filing volume is a forward-looking indicator of enforcement pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of settlements and judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: In total, 558 FCA settlements and judgments were entered in FY 2024, second only to FY 2023’s all-time record of 566 recoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count of settlements/judgments complements dollar totals to show enforcement activity frequency; use year-to-year comparisons to indicate trend strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pandemic-related fraud recoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: Recoveries for pandemic-related fraud (e.g., improper PPP payments and fraudulent COVID-19 tests/treatment) totaled more than $250 million in FY 2024, up from $48.3 million in FY 2023. Significant examples include a $120 million claim in the Kabbage bankruptcy and a $14.3 million payment from a lab related to forged physician signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing thematic enforcement, isolate pandemic-related recoveries and cite exemplar matters; compare to prior-year totals to show persistence or decline of pandemic-era enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government contractor/procurement fraud recoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: DOJ highlighted a settlement with Raytheon Company (finalized in FY 2025) as the second largest FCA government procurement fraud recovery ever — resolving allegations of double billing on a weapons maintenance contract and knowingly providing false information to the Department of Defense during contract negotiations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For procurement risk analysis, flag large contractor settlements and the alleged misconduct (e.g., double billing, false statements during negotiations) as precedent for government-contractor enforcement exposure. Note timing of finalization relative to fiscal-year boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Cybersecurity Fraud Initiative enforcement categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Civil Cybersecurity Fraud Initiative (launched 2021), DOJ uses the FCA to enforce contractual cybersecurity requirements and has taken action where vendors allegedly (1) provide deficient cybersecurity products or services; (2) misrepresent their cybersecurity practices or protocols; or (3) fail to monitor and report cybersecurity incidents or breaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating cybersecurity compliance risk in government contracting, assess contractual cybersecurity representations, product/service adequacy, and incident-monitoring/reporting obligations. DOJ has obtained substantial settlements from contractors, service providers, and academic institutions under this initiative and is expected to continue using the FCA in this area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti‑Kickback and opioid-related enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: DOJ continued to pursue violations of the Anti‑Kickback Statute, securing millions to resolve allegations of kickbacks (from commission-based referrals to travel and lavish dinners). DOJ also secured an agreement for a general unsecured claim of $475.6 million related to aggressive marketing of an opioid drug to high‑volume prescribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight intersections between FCA claims and other statutes (e.g., Anti‑Kickback Statute) and use large opioid-related resolutions as indicators of aggressive enforcement in pharmaceutical and provider conduct areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal-year timing and boundary effects on reported totals
rubrics_metrics.description: Some significant settlements occur just after fiscal-year close and may affect comparative totals (e.g., DOJ entered into a $425 million settlement with a generic drug manufacturer just after the close of FY 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing annual totals, note transactions finalized shortly after the fiscal-year cutoff and clarify whether such amounts are captured in the reported year or a subsequent year to avoid misinterpretation of trends.
